interface.title: EEG Quality Inspector
interface.stage_of_work: Data quality control before analysis (screening raw recordings)
interface.what_it_is_for: Load an EEG recording (the synthetic demo, a CSV or an EDF), look at the per-channel waveforms and spectrum, flag flat, clipped, high-amplitude and missing data over 1-second windows using thresholds you can change, and export an HTML report and a CSV metrics table, all on your own machine and without making any diagnostic claims.

data.source: built-in synthetic demo and uploaded test file
data.note: Used both the built-in synthetic demo (8 channels, 30 s, 256 Hz, seed 42, with planted flat/transient/clipped/line-noise/missing/high-amplitude/spiky channels) and the uploaded test file sample_eeg.csv (3 channels Fp1/Fp2/Cz, 60 rows), declared as 20 Hz and uV. No EDF test file was available, so the EDF uploader was never used.

tree.general: Screen a multichannel time-series recording for data-quality problems before analysis and record what was found

features.name: Stacked multichannel trace viewer with channel picker and time-range slider
features.general: Choose which signals to show, narrow the time range with a two-handle slider, then box-zoom and hover the shared-time-axis plot to read exact values; gaps in the data appear as breaks and dense data is reduced for display without losing peaks
features.specific: Waveforms tab: remove or add channel chips in the Channels multiselect, drag the Time window (s) handles, box-zoom the stacked Plotly traces, and hover to read (time, uV). Missing samples show as gaps, and display binning keeps the extremes
steps: remove or add channel chips
drag the start and end handles of the time window
drag a box on a trace to zoom
double-click to reset
hover a point to read time and amplitude
serves_tasks: View the raw traces per channel and look closely at suspect segments

features.name: Live threshold controls driving a per-channel flag table
features.general: Set numeric detection criteria in a side panel and watch the per-item flags table recompute right away without reloading the data, with a legend that restates the current criteria
features.specific: Sidebar section 2 (Flat window max p2p, Amplitude threshold, Clipping min run) feeds the Quality indicators table (flat_flag, amplitude_flag, clipping_flag), the How to read these indicators legend and the Active thresholds list
steps: type or step a threshold value
open Quality indicators to see the flags update
sort by a metric column or search for 'yes'
expand the legend to see the threshold now in use
serves_tasks: Read the per-channel flags for flat, missing, clipped and over-threshold data
Adjust the detection criteria and see the flags recompute

features.name: PSD spectrum with selectable line-noise ratio check
features.general: Plot the power spectrum of every channel and choose a contaminating frequency to get a per-channel ratio of power in the target band against neighboring bands; the check refuses to run when the frequency is above the Nyquist limit
features.specific: Spectrum tab: Welch PSD on a log axis with a toggleable legend, a Line-noise check select (off / 50 Hz / 60 Hz) that shows per-channel 'N.NNx' ratios (49–51 Hz vs 42–47 and 53–58 Hz), an excluded-windows note, and a Spectral parameters expander
steps: choose 50 Hz or 60 Hz in Line-noise check
read the per-channel ratio metrics
double-click a legend entry to show only that channel
expand Spectral parameters to see the method
serves_tasks: Compare each channel's power at the mains frequency against nearby frequencies
See how the check behaves when the sampling rate is too low to resolve the mains frequency

features.name: Data-source loader with declared sampling rate and unit conversion
features.general: Pick a demo dataset or upload a file, declare its sampling rate and physical units (the input is checked against limits), load it, and see a summary card that states the conversion that was applied and how many empty cells there were
features.specific: Sidebar section 1: Try the synthetic demo / Upload a file radio, CSV and EDF uploaders, CSV sampling rate (minimum 10 Hz), CSV units (uV / mV / V), and a Load button; the header shows channels, duration, Hz, samples, and a line such as 'declared in mV and converted to uV (factor 1000)'
steps: choose the input mode
upload a CSV
set the sampling rate
choose units
press Load and read the summary card
serves_tasks: Load a reference dataset with known defects to learn what each indicator looks like
Import your own recording, stating its sampling rate and measurement units
Check how a wrong unit declaration changes the results
Confirm that an implausible acquisition parameter is rejected
